record.paper_title: Some results and open problems in research on low dimensional organic conductors
record.original_question: Which effective theoretical description should be used for the electron gas in Bechgaard salts: a Luttinger-liquid description, a Fermi-liquid description, or a regime-dependent combination of the two? The paper notes that standard statistical mechanics predicts failure of the Fermi-liquid picture in strictly one-dimensional systems and favors the Luttinger-liquid model, while Bechgaard salts are physically quasi one-dimensional rather than exactly one-dimensional. The open problem is therefore to determine, with clear physical criteria, which model correctly describes these materials in which experimental situations.

evidence.quote: A very important and interesting problem in studies of Q1D organic metals is the choice of the theoretical model which can be applied to the electron gas: Luttinger or Fermi liquid?
However, the problem is open for further study, because there are numerous proofs and counter-proofs of both opinions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Bechgaard salts, a family of quasi-one-dimensional organic charge-transfer compounds of the form (TMTSF)$_2$X (with X an inorganic anion such as PF$_6$ or ClO$_4$). These materials consist of stacks of TMTSF molecules forming highly anisotropic conducting chains with intra-chain transfer integral $t_\parallel$ much larger than the inter-chain transfer integrals $t_\perp, t_{\perp\perp}$, so the electronic motion is strongly one-dimensional but not strictly so.

Two competing low-energy effective descriptions exist for the interacting electron gas in such a system:

(a) The Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid (TLL), the generic non-Fermi-liquid fixed point of interacting fermions in one spatial dimension, characterized by spin-charge separation, the absence of a coherent quasiparticle pole in the single-particle Green's function, and power-law decay of correlation functions with non-universal exponents controlled by a Luttinger parameter $K_\rho$.

(b) The Landau Fermi liquid (FL), the standard description in dimension $d\ge 2$, characterized by long-lived quasiparticles near the Fermi surface with a finite quasiparticle residue $Z>0$ and the usual analytic structure of the Green's function.

Formulate clear, quantitative physical criteria (in terms of temperature $T$, frequency $\omega$, wavevector, applied pressure, magnetic field, and the microscopic parameters $t_\parallel$, $t_\perp$, $t_{\perp\perp}$, on-site/extended Coulomb couplings, and the Luttinger parameter $K_\rho$) that determine in which experimentally accessible regimes the electron gas of the Bechgaard salts is correctly described by:

  (i) a pure Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid,
  (ii) a Landau Fermi liquid (possibly anisotropic), or
  (iii) a crossover/coexistence regime between the two,

and identify the dimensional-crossover scale $T^*$ (and the associated single-particle deconfinement scale) above which interchain coherence is lost and TLL behavior dominates, versus below which a higher-dimensional Fermi-liquid description becomes appropriate. Provide the criteria in a form that can be tested against transport, optical conductivity, NMR, and angle-resolved photoemission measurements.
artifact.category_tag: Luttinger vs Fermi liquid in quasi-1D conductors
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: optical and photoemission experiments support Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid behavior at high temperatures/energies in Bechgaard salts, and chain-DMFT and renormalization-group treatments capture a dimensional crossover at a scale T* (∼100 K for (TMTSF)$_2$PF$_6$, ≥200 K for (TMTSF)$_2$ClO$_4$) from a high-T Luttinger liquid to a low-T (anisotropic) Fermi liquid. However, a complete, quantitatively predictive theory unifying all experimental regimes (transport anomalies, pseudogap, role of interchain coupling and pressure) is still not fully settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Optical and photoemission evidence for a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid in the Bechgaard salts
status_evidence.snippet: Combined optical and photoemission experiments reveal the non-Fermi liquid character of these prototype quasi-one dimensional interacting electron systems.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental evidence supports a Luttinger-liquid description in part of the parameter range.

status_evidence.title: Electrodynamic properties of (TMTSF)2X
status_evidence.snippet: transition from a Luttinger-liquid to a Fermi-liquid behavior at the dimensional crossover when pressure is applied or temperature reduced
status_evidence.claim: A dimensional-crossover criterion between LL and FL exists and is controlled by temperature/pressure.

status_evidence.title: From Luttinger to Fermi Liquids in Organic Conductors
status_evidence.snippet: Chain-DMFT captures the metal-insulator transition and the dimensional crossover from a high temperature Luttinger liquid to a low temperature Fermi liquid phase; T*~100K for PF6, T*≥200K for ClO4.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative crossover scales have been identified via chain-DMFT, indicating partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-one-dimensional organic conductors: dimensional crossover and some puzzles
status_evidence.snippet: Dimensional crossover and unresolved puzzles in quasi-1D organic conductors.
status_evidence.claim: Open puzzles remain in the LL-to-FL crossover picture.
